title: Citing a record by its identifier makes that identifier's words searchable
problem: Judge whether a retrieval hit means the record is about the queried concept.
failure: An Arabic query for `قدرة` (capability) returned a number-theory card. The card is not about capability: its transfer field cites another record by id, `proxy-capability`, and the id's words entered the index as ordinary tokens. The hit is real text and a false concept match at the same time, so neither keeping it nor filtering the term is obviously right.
correction: Not fixed. Reported as a limitation of the lexical index with its mechanism named, because the obvious fixes each cost something: filtering id-shaped tokens would also hide genuine references, and excluding the citing field would lose real content. Measured and left visible rather than silently filtered.
transfer: Any index built over prose that contains identifiers of other records will retrieve on those identifiers. Cross-references are content to a tokeniser and metadata to a reader, and the tokeniser cannot tell which it is looking at.
limits: One engine, 7 live cards, one observed instance. No claim about how often this occurs, and no fix is proposed or verified.
author: CLAUDE
